description: Identification and clinical significance of ventricular arrhythmias
overview: This module covers ventricular arrhythmias including ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and premature ventricular contractions, focusing on recognition and clinical management.
objectives: Learn emergency management of ventricular arrhythmias

slides.title: Ventricular Tachycardia
slides.content: Ventricular tachycardia: wide QRS complexes (>0.12s), rate >100 bpm, regular rhythm, no P waves, hemodynamic instability possible. May be monomorphic or polymorphic. Sustained VT requires immediate treatment.

slides.title: Ventricular Fibrillation
slides.content: Ventricular fibrillation: chaotic, irregular rhythm, no identifiable QRS complexes, immediately life-threatening, requires defibrillation. Patient has no pulse and is unconscious.

quiz.question: What is the immediate treatment for ventricular fibrillation?
quiz.explanation: Ventricular fibrillation requires immediate defibrillation as it is immediately life-threatening.

slides.title: Premature Ventricular Contractions
slides.content: PVCs: wide QRS complexes, abnormal morphology, compensatory pause, may be benign or indicate underlying heart disease. Frequency and pattern determine clinical significance.

quiz.question: What characterizes a premature ventricular contraction?
quiz.explanation: PVCs are characterized by wide QRS complexes due to abnormal ventricular conduction.

slides.title: Torsades de Pointes
slides.content: Torsades de Pointes: polymorphic VT with QRS axis twisting, associated with prolonged QT interval. May be drug-induced or congenital. Emergency treatment includes magnesium and defibrillation.

quiz.question: What is the characteristic feature of Torsades de Pointes?
quiz.explanation: Torsades de Pointes is characterized by polymorphic VT with QRS axis twisting around the baseline.

slides.title: Emergency Management
slides.content: Emergency management: assess patient stability, immediate defibrillation for VF/pulseless VT, antiarrhythmic drugs for stable VT, address underlying causes, consider ICD placement for survivors.

quiz.question: What is the first priority in managing unstable ventricular tachycardia?
quiz.explanation: Unstable ventricular tachycardia requires immediate cardioversion to restore circulation.
